title: Pick two apples off a potted apple tree by lifting, stems on, and lay them in a picking bucket
instruction: Pick both apples off the tree into the bucket.
context: Picking apples into a bucket is familiar from gardens and pick-your-own orchards. A picker frees each apple from its spur with the stem still on it, holds it without squeezing hard enough to bruise it, and lays it down rather than dropping it. A straight pull can pull the stem out of the fruit, which shortens how long it keeps. This reusable practice rig stands in for the tree: each apple hangs from a magnetic stem cap on its spur, and a second magnetic joint holds the stem in the apple. Rolling the apple up and drawing it away frees the cap with the stem on; a straight pull along the stem can pull the stem out instead. The apples are then laid in a padded bucket without being dropped.
setup: The real-world version is a reusable practice rig. World x forward, y left, z up; table top is z=0 in these setup dimensions. A 25 mm hardwood-dowel artificial trunk rises 500 mm above the table from a 300 mm, 12 L black pot of dry sand and bark mulch, 11.5 kg total. Pot centre is (0.350,-0.100) m. Two printed 25 mm spurs point at azimuths 160 and 250 degrees, carrying 75 mm rubber-coated imitation apples whose complete handled socket/peg/stem/cap assemblies total 180 g with centred COMs at heights 310 and 350 mm. Their centres are approximately (0.273,-0.072) and (0.322,-0.177) m. Each has a 6 x 20 mm TPU95A flexible stem, nominal 19-degree precurve, 12.7 x 3 mm steel cap on a D84 spur magnet (session-check target 40 N) and a 12 mm peg on a D82 socket magnet (24 N). A 16 mm diameter, 30 mm deep open well recesses the 16 x 16.7 mm socket mouth 13 mm below the shoulder; the stem above the socket is not buried. A hollow apple/internal cavity is accessed through a 20 mm calyx port for centred epoxy-secured steel ballast. A 290 mm diameter, 230 mm deep green bucket with 25 mm foam pad stands at (0.200,-0.430) m. Both arms start READY, grippers open; task-local native effort limits are 40 N per finger. CAD, assembly and proposed physical session checks are in README.md and rig/.
scoring: Measured with a ruler, from a photo, from the video and from the robot's gripper log. An apple is in the bucket when it rests inside it: its centre inside the bucket's wall (by at least half the apple's radius) and below the rim, sitting on the foam pad or on the other apple (its centre within 1 cm of where it would rest on them). It was dropped if it was let go (no gripper touching it), or came off the tree with no gripper touching it, with its lowest point more than 5 cm above what it then landed on (the pad, the other apple, the pot's soil or rim, the bucket's rim or the table); or if, with no gripper touching it, it came down onto the table from more than 5 cm above it since it was last held or at rest (rolling off the bucket's rim, say); or if it reached the floor. It was bruised if a finger ever pressed on it with more than 24 N (the lowest compression force reported to damage ripe apples): in the simulation, each finger pad's contact force along its closing direction, read every control step; on the real YAM, the gripper's clamping force in its log (motor torque converted to finger force as the YAM's driver does for its gripper force limit). Its stem is on when the stem (with its steel cap) is still in the apple; it is a stem pull when the apple came off without it (the stem stays on the spur). 0 at any moment, and it stays 0: the pot tips over (leans more than 20 degrees from upright). Otherwise, by the state at the end, each apple earns: 0.5 if it is in the bucket, its stem is on, and it was neither dropped nor bruised; 0.25 if it is in the bucket and was neither dropped nor bruised, but its stem pulled out (a stem pull); 0 otherwise: still on the tree, dropped, bruised, or outside the bucket. The task score is the sum for the two apples, and 1.0 also needs no gripper touching an apple and both apples still (no point of either apple moving more than 5 mm over the last 1 s), held for 1 s; otherwise the sum is capped at 0.75. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Return pot and bucket to their tape marks, empty the bucket, push pulled-out pegs back into their sockets and reseat both magnetic stem caps. No part is consumed. Before each session, and after changing a magnet, steel disc, shim or stem, run the release checks in rig/release-checks.md with a luggage scale (1 N steps) and a side-view phone video. Use the rig only when every reading is inside its band: the cap pulled straight off the spur at 40 +- 3 N; the apple pulled off its peg at 24 +- 2 N; a straight pull on the hanging apple pulling the peg first at 24 +- 2 N; a downward pull at the apple's centre releasing the cap at 5.5 +- 1.5 N; the apple level within 5 degrees, drooping a further 11 +- 3 degrees with 100 g added. Add 0.1 mm paper shims to lower a hold that is too strong; replace a weak magnet or disc.
fidelity: Real-size practice rig. Cap frees at 40 N tension plus bend/6.35 mm; peg (stem pull) at 24 N. In an 18 N pinch, roll-and-draw freed both caps at about 18.6 N; straight pulls freed one cap at 20.6 N and pulled one stem out at 24 N, near ripe-apple picks (15-16 N field, 24-28 N straight). Sideways release (about 7 N) is below their 12-14 N. Loads are design targets, not measured on a built rig. Rigid rubber-coated apples (friction 1.2) grip better than real skin; bruise = finger over 24 N.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 controls). Scripted demo: 1.0 (1,633 controls). Straight-pull counterexample: 0.75 (1,281). Squeeze counterexample: 0.5 (1,833).
